questions.question: Discuss on passive transport?
questions.solution_html:
• Passive Transport –
  • Definition - (2 marks)
  • Types – (3 marks) for each type
  • • No energy required; occurs down the concentration gradient (high to low concentration).
  • • Naturally occurring process; cell does not use energy.
  • • Main types: Simple diffusion, Facilitated diffusion, and Osmosis.
  • Simple Diffusion
  • • Random movement of particles from high to low concentration.
  • • Continues until equilibrium (even distribution) is reached.
  • Facilitated Diffusion
  • • Movement of ions or polar molecules with the help of membrane proteins.
  • • Uses transmembrane integral proteins to allow passage.
  • • No energy used; relies on concentration gradient.
  • • Proteins protect molecules from the membrane's hydrophobic core.
  • Osmosis
  • • Diffusion of water through a semi-permeable membrane.
  • • Water moves from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
  • • Movement is inversely related to solute concentration.
questions.final_answer: • Movement is inversely related to solute concentration.

  • diffusion
  • Lower temperature → decreases molecular energy → slower diffusion
  • • Solubility
  • Nonpolar/lipid-soluble substances diffuse faster than polar substances
  • • Concentration Gradient
  • Greater concentration difference → faster diffusion
  • • Mass of Molecules
  • Heavier molecules → move slowly → slower diffusion
  • Lighter molecules → move faster → faster diffusion
  • • Density of Solvent
  • Higher density → slower diffusion (more resistance to movement)
  • Lower density → faster diffusion
  • • Surface Area / Membrane Thickness
  • Increased surface area → faster diffusion
  • Thicker membrane → slower diffusion
  • • Distance Travelled
  • Greater distance → slower diffusion
  • Shorter distance → faster diffusion
questions.final_answer: Shorter distance → faster diffusion
